name: Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation with Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation
description: Mobile ALOHA is a robotic imitation learning benchmark and demonstration dataset for whole-body bimanual mobile manipulation. Developed at Stanford University, the platform mounts two ViperX 300 6-DoF robot arms onto an AgileX Tracer omnidirectional mobile base, controlled by a low-cost untethered teleoperation harness. The dataset consists of 320 real-world expert mobile manipulation demonstrations across 7 complex, long-horizon domestic tasks (including wiping spilled wine, cooking shrimp, rinsing pans, serving food, and navigating elevators). The dataset establishes a proven co-training methodology that integrates 825 existing static tabletop ALOHA demonstrations to bootstrap autonomous mobile manipulation with high data efficiency.

verification.notes: Verified against mobile-aloha.github.io, src.stanford.edu showcase, and arXiv:2401.02117 paper. Confirmed 320 real mobile demonstrations across 7 tasks and co-training relationship with 825 static ALOHA demonstrations.

size.notes: Recorded as HDF5 files containing 4 camera video streams (overhead, front, left wrist, right wrist) and whole-body joint and velocity trajectories.

citation.paper_title: Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation with Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation

provenance.collection_method: Direct physical whole-body teleoperation using an operator-strapped exoskeleton master controlling twin puppet arms and an omnidirectional base.
provenance.curation_notes: Features 7 challenging mobile tasks. Uses a co-training pipeline where mini-batches are drawn equally from the 320 mobile demonstrations and the 825 static tabletop ALOHA demonstrations.
data_sources: Original recordings at Stanford University Robotics Center
